prompt:
Build a useful offline incident-triage CLI from scratch in this empty workspace. Use Python 3.12 standard library only; no downloads or dependencies. Deliver triage.py, README.md and tests/test_triage.py. Implement first rather than repeatedly exploring an empty directory.

Interface: python triage.py --store PATH COMMAND (default store incidents.json). Commands: add TITLE --severity critical|high|medium|low (default medium); list --status all|open|closed (default all), optionally --severity; close ID; summary. Successful commands output JSON only to stdout. Add and close output one incident object containing positive increasing integer id, trimmed nonempty title, severity and status (open or closed). List outputs an array sorted by severity critical, high, medium, low then ascending id. Summary outputs exactly {open: count, closed: count, by_severity: {critical: open_count, high: open_count, medium: open_count, low: open_count}}.

Persist across separate CLI processes using UTF-8 JSON. Never reuse IDs. Create missing parent directories for writes. Save atomically using a temporary file and replace. Reading a missing store returns empty results without creating the store. Closing an already closed incident succeeds idempotently. Unknown IDs, whitespace-only titles, invalid severities, malformed JSON or invalid store schemas must exit nonzero, explain the problem on stderr without a traceback, and leave existing store bytes unchanged. Preserve Unicode. Provide --help and practical README command examples. Write at least six meaningful unittest tests and run python -m unittest discover -s tests -v. Use temporary stores in tests. Do not claim checks passed unless you ran them. Finish with a concise statement of implemented behavior and checks run.
